title: Lead Finder
description: Pick what you're looking for; the finder pulls businesses, reads their sites for contact details and keeps as many ready leads as you can write to each week.

form.title: New lead search

form.categoryHint: Pick a Google Business category from the suggestions.
form.noCategories: No matching categories. Try a shorter word.
form.locationHint: Small typos are fine. If the name matches several places, you pick one.
form.pickLocation: Several places match. Pick the one you mean:
form.noLocations: No place found. Check the spelling or add the city or country.
form.costNote: Pulling businesses uses a small amount of credits. Reading websites and checking emails is free.

detail.shownStores: Showing {{count}} sites that couldn't be confirmed as live Shopify stores.

phrases.description: The sentences your emails use to describe each lead's gaps. Rewrite them in your own voice; {detail} is replaced with a number or date where one exists. Keep each one readable on its own, since it is also used in bullet lists.

templates.title: Email templates
templates.description: Templates fill in each lead's name, first line, website and biggest gap. The email opens ready to send in your mail app.
templates.empty: No templates yet. Start with the Turkish and English samples: a first email and two follow-ups. Edit them in your own voice; a business address is required in US cold emails.

templates.subject: Subject

findingWhy.no_website: Customers who find them on Maps have nowhere to read more, compare or buy, so they go to a competitor with a site.
findingWhy.unclaimed_profile: Anyone can suggest edits to an unclaimed profile, and the owner can't reply to reviews, add photos or posts.
findingWhy.few_reviews: Fewer than 10 reviews makes people hesitate and keeps the business lower in local results.
findingWhy.low_rating: Most people filter out businesses under 4 stars; a review strategy and replies can lift it.
findingWhy.no_hours: Google shows these businesses less for "open now" searches and people call less.
findingWhy.few_photos: Listings with more photos get more clicks and direction requests.
findingWhy.no_click_to_call: Most local visitors are on phones; a number they can't tap means lost calls.
findingWhy.no_online_booking: Clinics, salons and studios lose bookings outside office hours without online booking.
findingWhy.noindex_home: A noindex tag tells Google not to show the page at all. Usually a leftover from building the site.
findingWhy.no_https: Browsers mark the site as not secure and visitors leave, especially at checkout or forms.
findingWhy.http_not_redirected: Two versions of the site split Google's signals and some visitors land on the insecure one.
findingWhy.not_mobile_friendly: No mobile layout tag, so the site likely shows tiny text on phones, where most traffic comes from.
findingWhy.weak_title: The title is the blue headline on Google. A generic one like "Home" wastes the most important SEO spot.
findingWhy.no_meta_description: Google writes its own snippet, often a random piece of text, which gets fewer clicks.
findingWhy.h1_issue: The page has no main heading or several, so Google gets a weaker signal about the topic.
findingWhy.no_canonical: Without it, duplicate URLs (filters, tracking links) can compete with each other in Google.
findingWhy.missing_alt: Image descriptions bring Google Images traffic and help accessibility.
findingWhy.no_sitemap: A sitemap helps Google find and refresh every page, especially new products or posts.
findingWhy.no_open_graph: Links shared on WhatsApp, Instagram or Facebook show no image, so fewer people click.
findingWhy.no_lang: Search engines and screen readers have to guess the language of the page.
findingWhy.thin_content: Very little text gives Google and AI assistants little to understand and rank.
findingWhy.no_hreflang: Without hreflang, Google may show the wrong language version to visitors abroad.
findingWhy.heavy_page: Very large HTML usually means a slow page, which costs both rankings and sales.
findingWhy.unoptimized_images: All images load at once with no responsive sizes, slowing the first view on phones.
findingWhy.too_many_scripts: Many outside scripts (apps, widgets, trackers) slow the site. Common on stores with many apps.
findingWhy.ai_bots_blocked: robots.txt stops ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Google AI from reading the site, so they can't recommend it.
findingWhy.no_schema: No schema markup at all, so Google and AI get no clean facts like prices, hours or ratings.
findingWhy.no_org_schema: Organization or LocalBusiness data tells AI assistants who the business is, where it is and how to reach it.
findingWhy.no_faq: FAQ sections answer the exact questions people ask AI assistants, and get quoted.
findingWhy.no_review_schema: Without rating markup, star ratings don't appear next to the site in Google.
findingWhy.no_llms_txt: A small, new standard that gives AI assistants a summary of the site. Nice to have.
findingWhy.no_blog: No regular SEO blog. Articles are the main way to win informational searches and get cited in AI answers, so this is critical.
findingWhy.stale_blog: A blog that stopped months ago looks abandoned and stops bringing new traffic. Regular posting is critical for SEO and AI visibility.
findingWhy.irregular_blog: Fewer than 2 posts in the last 3 months. Regular SEO posts are critical for Google and AI visibility; irregular publishing stalls growth.
findingWhy.myshopify_domain: Running on the default address hurts trust and brand recall; a custom domain is a quick win.
findingWhy.vintage_theme: Vintage themes lack Online Store 2.0: no sections on every page, fewer app blocks, slower.
findingWhy.stock_theme: A free default theme makes the store look like thousands of others. A custom design is the pitch.
findingWhy.old_copyright: An outdated year in the footer makes the business look inactive.
findingWhy.powered_by_shopify: A small default leftover that signals the store setup was never finished.
findingWhy.no_favicon: No icon in browser tabs and some search results; looks unfinished.
findingWhy.legacy_analytics: Universal Analytics stopped collecting data in July 2023, so they likely have no traffic data now.
findingWhy.no_analytics: No GA4 or Tag Manager visible, so they can't see where visitors come from or what sells.
findingWhy.no_meta_pixel: Facebook and Instagram ads can't retarget visitors or optimize for sales.
findingWhy.no_google_ads_tag: If they run Google Ads, conversions aren't measured, so the budget is spent blind.
findingWhy.no_tiktok_pixel: No way to run measurable TikTok ads or build audiences from visitors.
findingWhy.no_pinterest_tag: For visual products, Pinterest ads can't track sales without the tag.
findingWhy.no_heatmap: No Clarity or Hotjar, so they can't see where visitors get stuck. Clarity is free.
findingWhy.no_consent_banner: In the EU and UK, Google Ads needs Consent Mode; without it, conversion data and remarketing break.
findingWhy.no_email_marketing: No signup form or email platform detected, so likely no welcome or abandoned cart emails. Confirm with the owner before pitching.
findingWhy.mailchimp_store: Mailchimp has weak e-commerce flows and segmentation; a Klaviyo migration is a strong pitch.
findingWhy.no_spf: Without SPF, their own emails (orders, newsletters) are more likely to go to spam.
findingWhy.no_dmarc: Gmail and Yahoo require DMARC for bulk senders since 2024; newsletters may be rejected.
findingWhy.free_email_contact: A free email address looks less professional than one on their own domain.
findingWhy.no_reviews_app: Product reviews are one of the biggest conversion levers; no review app was visible.
findingWhy.no_live_chat: A quick way to ask before buying or booking turns hesitant visitors into customers.
findingWhy.out_of_stock: A large share of the sampled products are sold out, which wastes traffic and ad spend.
findingWhy.empty_descriptions: Products without descriptions rank poorly and give shoppers and AI nothing to go on.
findingWhy.single_image_products: One photo per product lowers conversion; shoppers want angles, details and scale.
findingWhy.stale_products: No new products in over a year can mean an inactive store or a stale catalog.
findingWhy.no_product_schema: Google Shopping and Merchant Center read product data from this markup. Without it, free listings and rich results suffer.
findingWhy.product_schema_gaps: Missing fields like GTIN, brand or availability are common reasons for Merchant Center warnings and disapprovals.
findingWhy.no_social_links: Visitors can't check social proof, and AI assistants get fewer signals about the brand.
findingWhy.no_about_page: People and AI assistants look for who is behind a business before trusting it.
findingWhy.no_privacy_policy: Required by law in most markets and by ad platforms like Google and Meta.
findingWhy.no_refund_policy: Shoppers check returns before buying, and Merchant Center requires a return policy.
findingWhy.no_kvkk: Turkish sites collecting personal data need a KVKK disclosure; missing it is a legal risk.
